hints: Apply the Binomial Theorem $(a+b)^4 = \sum_{r=0}^4 \binom{4}{r} a^{4-r}b^r$ with $a=2x$ and $b=-\frac{3}{x}$.
Carefully calculate powers and signs for each term, tracking both the negative signs and powers of $x$.
Simplify all coefficients and write out all five terms in descending powers of $x$.
walkthrough:
Apply the Binomial Theorem $(a+b)^4 = \sum_{r=0}^4 \binom{4}{r} a^{4-r}b^r$ with $a = 2x$ and $b = -\frac{3}{x}$:
$$\left(2x - \frac{3}{x}\right)^4 = \binom{4}{0}(2x)^4 + \binom{4}{1}(2x)^3\left(-\frac{3}{x}\right) + \binom{4}{2}(2x)^2\left(-\frac{3}{x}\right)^2 + \binom{4}{3}(2x)\left(-\frac{3}{x}\right)^3 + \binom{4}{4}\left(-\frac{3}{x}\right)^4$$

Compute each term step-by-step using binomial coefficients $1, 4, 6, 4, 1$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Term 1: } & 1 \times 16x^4 = 16x^4 \\ \text{Term 2: } & 4 \times (8x^3) \times \left(-\frac{3}{x}\right) = -96x^2 \\ \text{Term 3: } & 6 \times (4x^2) \times \left(\frac{9}{x^2}\right) = 216 \\ \text{Term 4: } & 4 \times (2x) \times \left(-\frac{27}{x^3}\right) = -216x^{-2} \\ \text{Term 5: } & 1 \times \left(\frac{81}{x^4}\right) = 81x^{-4} \end{aligned}$$

Combine all five terms to give the complete simplified expansion:
$$16x^4 - 96x^2 + 216 - 216x^{-2} + 81x^{-4}$$

hints: Substitute your expansion from part (a) into $(x^2+5)\left(2x-\frac{3}{x}\right)^4$.
Identify which pairs of terms multiply to produce an $x^2$ term: $x^2 \times (\text{constant term})$ and $5 \times (x^2 \text{ term})$.
Add these two terms together to determine the final numerical coefficient of $x^2$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the binomial expansion from part (a) into the product:
$$\left(x^2 + 5\right)\left(16x^4 - 96x^2 + 216 - 216x^{-2} + 81x^{-4}\right)$$

Identify the pairs of terms that multiply to produce an $x^2$ term:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 \times (\text{constant term}): &\quad x^2 \times 216 = 216x^2 \\ 5 \times (x^2 \text{ term}): &\quad 5 \times (-96x^2) = -480x^2 \end{aligned}$$

Sum the contributions to find the total $x^2$ term:
$$216x^2 - 480x^2 = (216 - 480)x^2 = -264x^2$$
